concerns.concern: The relaxation-rate argument does not rule out heating. Joule heating during the pump followed by fast turn-off is itself a thermal quench, which would give a stronger effect at faster ramps despite less deposited energy. A stage thermometer cannot detect millisecond local heating.
concerns.quote: Pump-induced heating followed by rapid turn-off is itself a thermal quench, so it would naturally produce the observed α-dependence and the low-T enhancement.

concerns.concern: The field range of the memory effect does not match the claimed SC1/SC2 coexistence region. In sample S2 the effect peaks near 10 T and vanishes by about 17 T, deep in what calorimetry identifies as pure SC1. Extended Data Fig. 9, cited for S2, actually shows S1.
concerns.quote: In S2 the effect peaks near 10 T and vanishes around 17 T, well below the SC1→SC2 boundary and outside the 15–20 T coexistence window

concerns.concern: A 1D noisy overdamped Langevin model in a periodic potential has a unique stationary V(J). It therefore cannot produce two distinct asymptotic branches unless an unspecified finite observation time is used.
concerns.quote: A 1D noisy Langevin system in a periodic potential has a unique stationary V(J), so two asymptotic branches are not possible.

concerns.concern: Without noise, the deterministic dynamics would trap the phase in the higher-Jc π well during up-sweeps and slow ramp-downs. This is the opposite of the claimed protocol outcomes (pump gives π, slow erase gives 0), so the result must rely on unreported tuned noise and time scales.
concerns.quote: Deterministic overdamped dynamics would trap the phase in the higher-Jc π well during slow ramps, the opposite of what is claimed.

concerns.concern: The strong low-temperature enhancement is not a good argument against heating. Heat capacity and thermal conductance fall at low T, so heating excursions and quenches are larger at 50 mK. Thermally activated creep would also erase metastable pinning states near 0.6 K.
concerns.quote: Labelling this the 'strongest' argument against heating seems unjustified.

concerns.concern: The claim that Bean critical-state pinning is insensitive to turn-off speed is wrong. Conventional vortex matter shows strong rate-dependent metastability (flux creep, peak-effect disordered states). Turn-off sensitivity therefore does not distinguish intrinsic UTe2 physics from conventional pinning.
concerns.quote: The observed turn-off-speed sensitivity is therefore not evidence for intrinsic UTe2-specific physics over conventional pinning-driven metastability.

concerns.concern: The role of disorder is untested. Most data come from the lowest-RRR sample, and the cleanest sample (RRR 395) was not given pump/erase tests. This is the most direct way to separate an intrinsic mechanism from disorder-driven vortex-glass metastability.
concerns.quote: Whether the effect grows, shrinks or vanishes with disorder is the most direct way to separate an intrinsic order-parameter mechanism from disorder-driven vortex-glass metastability

concerns.concern: Comparing the 0.6 K memory onset with the zero-field Tc of 2.1 K overstates the separation of energy scales. The relevant comparison is with Tc(B) at 14 T and with the creep scale at that field, so the inference of an intrinsic low-energy phenomenon is unsupported.
concerns.quote: The relevant comparison is with Tc(B=14 T) and with the irreversibility/creep scale at that field, not with 2.1 K.

concerns.concern: The simulated φ(t) in Extended Data Fig. 2c,d shows overshoot and damped oscillations. These are impossible for the stated first-order, no-capacitance equation, so it is unclear which equation was actually integrated.
concerns.quote: An overdamped first-order equation cannot produce the ringing shown in Extended Data Fig. 2c.

concerns.concern: The Methods says γ is used as a proxy for the injected current J, although γ is defined as the damping. This is either a typo or means the horizontal axis of the simulated J–V curves is not the drive current.
concerns.quote: Saying γ is a proxy for J in constructing the J–V curves is either a typo or suggests the horizontal axis of Fig. 3c

concerns.concern: In the overdamped model the critical current is set by the potential slope (β), not by the damping γ. Attributing the higher Jc of the memory state to larger damping from domain walls conflates two independent model ingredients.
concerns.quote: This conflates two independent model ingredients.

concerns.concern: The model cannot be reproduced. The values of g, the noise amplitude, the pulse amplitudes, durations and ramp rates in model units, the integration scheme and the averaging window are all missing, as are the resulting Jc0 and Jcπ values.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3c and Extended Data Fig. 2 cannot be reproduced.

concerns.concern: Non-volatility over several hours is asserted but no retention data (ΔJ versus waiting time) are shown. It is therefore unclear whether the state slowly relaxes or is erased by the probe sweeps.
concerns.quote: non-volatility for hours (no data shown)

concerns.concern: The claim that read/write is purely superconducting is false. The write pulse drives the sample deep into flux flow with tens to hundreds of µV, and reading the low-Jc state also gives a finite voltage. The ~1 nW figure covers reading only.
concerns.quote: purely superconducting read/write (the write pulse drives flux flow)

concerns.concern: Describing the effect as controlled solely by electrical stimuli, in contrast to field-based schemes, ignores that operation needs a static 7–20 T field along b within ~20° and temperatures below about 0.4 K.
concerns.quote: 'solely electrical' control (a 7–20 T field and ~50 mK are required)

concerns.concern: The power comparison with nanometre-sized silicon elements cites ref. 59, a 1990 paper on intrinsic carrier concentration in silicon. That paper does not address the power consumption of memory elements.
concerns.quote: the power comparison to silicon (supported by an irrelevant citation)

concerns.concern: The model predicts a lower flux-flow resistance in the memory state, but the data do not show this. The out-of-equilibrium curves rejoin the equilibrium ones with similar or steeper slope.
concerns.quote: The predicted lower flux-flow resistance in the memory state is also not evident in the data.

concerns.concern: The model gives only a binary outcome. It does not simulate the graded, saturating dependence of ΔJ on pump amplitude, duration and relaxation rate, so its claim to capture the phenomenology is limited.
concerns.quote: The graded, saturating dependence of ΔJ on amplitude, duration and α (Extended Data Fig. 1) is not simulated

concerns.concern: The erase protocol in Fig. 1d,e appears as a rectangular intermediate-amplitude block. This conflicts with the described smooth-ramp erasure, and the erase polarity differs between the caption and the Methods.
concerns.quote: the erase appears as a rectangular block of intermediate amplitude (~4 A cm⁻²)

concerns.concern: The Methods description of the Fig. 1d pulse sequence is too vague to reproduce. The sample cross-sections and contact spacings needed to convert mA to A cm⁻² are not given.
concerns.quote: The Methods description of the Fig. 1d sequence is too vague to reproduce, and the sample cross-sections needed to convert mA to A cm⁻² are not given.

concerns.concern: ΔJ magnitudes are inconsistent across figures, and the voltage criterion used is often not stated. It is therefore unclear whether the field dependence and peak location in Fig. 4e are real or an artifact of the criterion.
concerns.quote: it is unclear whether the field dependence in Fig. 4e is a real trend or an artifact of the chosen V

concerns.concern: The fidelity of microsecond pulses and fast ramps is not demonstrated. 10 µs pulses with 100 points may exceed the Keithley 6221's arbitrary-waveform capability, and lead inductance may distort the waveforms. Yet the duration and rate dependences are key evidence.
concerns.quote: the actual waveforms at the sample should be verified

concerns.concern: The memory state is called non-transient in one place but metastable or a long-lived transient elsewhere. The terminology is inconsistent.
concerns.quote: The abstract calls it 'a metastable state', and Methods calls it 'a long-lived transient (metastable) state'.

concerns.concern: Inversion symmetry alone allows metastable minima at ±φ0. Forcing φ = π requires assuming the metastable state is itself inversion invariant, which is not stated or tied to the supporting data. The implied period-2L modulation is also left implicit.
concerns.quote: Only the stronger assumption that the metastable state itself is inversion-invariant forces φ0 = π (mod 2π).

concerns.concern: The text contains thermodynamic misstatements. Equilibrium minimises free energy, not entropy, and pinning is a vortex–defect effect, not something acting between vortices.
concerns.quote: Equilibrium minimises free energy F = E − TS.

concerns.concern: There is a notational slip in the model description: 'the global minimum at π = 0' should read φ = 0.
concerns.quote: 'The global minimum at 𝜋 = 0' should read 𝜙 = 0.
